1.title: The Quality Practice in Context
1.text: Welcome to Module six: The Quality Practice in Context. It covers the exam area The prince two practices. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Apply the quality practice: product description, product register, quality management approach, quality register. Areas of focus of key roles. Quality planning, control, assurance, review and acceptance. Analyze whether a quality approach is effective and fit for purpose considering the principles, the techniques and tailoring. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two practices (fifty-one percent). Exam format: an open-book scenario exam: one hundred fifty minutes, seventy marks, forty-two marks to pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Practitioner syllabus (people cert), version seven point two.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and principles
1.text: Purpose, objectives and principles. The quality practice makes sure the project creates products that are fit for purpose and that the users can accept. It starts from the user quality expectations (what the customer side expects) and turns them into acceptance criteria and quality criteria that can be checked. It serves mainly focus on products: quality is defined product by product before building. It also serves continued business justification (benefits depend on usable products), define roles, responsibilities and relationships (who checks, who assures, who accepts), manage by stages (quality is reviewed at each boundary) and tailor to suit the project.

1.title: Purpose, objectives and principles, continued
1.text: Purpose, objectives and principles. The figure shows this: Quality planning, quality control, quality assurance and acceptance around a product. Exam tip: Quality is defined before the product is built, not after. If a scenario writes the criteria after the work is finished, the approach is not fit for purpose.

1.title: The key management products
1.text: The key management products. Product description. One product: purpose, composition, derivation, format, quality criteria and how it will be checked and by whom. Product register. A record of the products, their status and their approval. Quality management approach. How quality will be achieved on this project: standards, methods, roles, records and acceptance. Part of the initiation documentation. Quality register. A record of every planned and completed quality check, with who, when and the result. The project product description (Module five) holds the user quality expectations and acceptance criteria for the whole project. Exam tip: Quality register records checks; product register records products and approvals. Pick by the verb: checked and result means quality register, approved and status means product register.

1.title: Areas of focus of the key roles
1.text: Areas of focus of the key roles. Executive. Quality is affordable and supports the business case. Senior user. Gives the user quality expectations and acceptance criteria; provides user reviewers; confirms users accept the products. Senior supplier. Supplier standards and quality system are used; products meet the specification. Project manager. Plans quality and applies the quality management approach; keeps the records. Team manager. Quality control within work packages; reports results. Project assurance. Independent checks that the quality approach is followed and working. Project support. Maintains the registers. The board gives the final acceptance of the project product at closure. Check the book's table for exact wording.

1.title: Effective management and techniques
1.text: Effective management and techniques. Quality planning. Agree expectations, acceptance criteria, quality criteria, tolerances, methods and roles; write product descriptions before work starts. Quality control. Check the product against its criteria with tests, inspections or reviews; record results and follow up defects. Quality assurance. Independent assessment that the quality approach is followed and will meet needs; not done by the producer. Quality review. A planned check of a product by chosen reviewers against its criteria, with recorded findings and follow-up. Acceptance. Formal confirmation, by the person named in the product description, that the product meets its acceptance criteria.

1.title: Effective management and techniques, continued
1.text: Effective management and techniques. Quality control happens during delivery. Quality assurance runs alongside the project and reports to the board. Rework needs time in the plan, and approval is recorded in the product register. Exam tip: The person who made the product does not judge it. If the author, or the project manager, approves a product for the users, look for the independent reviewer or the senior user.

1.title: Judging a scenario
1.text: Judging a scenario. Criteria in product descriptions before building (focus on products). Criteria invented after delivery, or only "it works". Independent reviewers and testers. The author checks their own work. Every check recorded in the quality register with result. Checks done but not recorded, or recorded only at the end. Acceptance by the right person (senior user for user needs). Project manager or supplier accepts on the users' behalf.

1.title: Judging a scenario, continued
1.text: Judging a scenario. Assurance independent of the project manager. Project manager assures their own project. Quality checks and rework scheduled in the stage plan. Quality squeezed into the last week with no rework time. Findings used for lessons (learn from experience). Same defects repeat stage after stage.

1.title: Judging a scenario, continued
1.text: Judging a scenario. Tailoring. Small internal project. A short quality approach; one combined register. Agile or hybrid delivery. Acceptance criteria on each backlog item; user accepts each increment; team's definition of done is recorded. Large or multi-party project. Acceptance criteria in contracts; assurance of each supplier's quality system. Sustainability or data concerns. Quality criteria include energy use, materials or data quality and security. Exam tip: Tailoring scales the paperwork, not the independence. A short quality approach is fine; an unrecorded self-check by the author is not.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A developer in Wei Chen's team tests his own payment component, finds no faults and marks it approved in the product register. There is no other check. Was this appropriate? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: No, because the author should not judge the product and the check must be recorded. Quality control should be independent of the author and recorded in the quality register, as focus on products and assurance require.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. When Project Harbor closes, who should confirm on behalf of the users that the online permit service meets its acceptance criteria? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Tomas Reyes, senior user. The senior user speaks for the users and confirms acceptance; assurance is independent, the supplier built it and the project manager does not accept for users.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. The build stage is about to start, and the quality management approach requires independent reviews. Sam Okafor finds the stage's product descriptions have no quality criteria. What should he do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Get the criteria written and agreed with users before authorizing any work. Criteria must exist and be agreed before building starts, otherwise quality control has nothing to check against.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Sam Okafor wants one record of every planned and completed check on Project Harbor, with dates, reviewers and results. Which management product holds it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Quality register. The quality register records each quality check and its result; the product register records products and approvals, and a product description defines one product.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Aisha Bello, project assurance, sees that all checks of the payment component were done by the supplier's own team. She tells the board the approach is not independent enough and suggests an independent reviewer. Was this appropriate? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Yes, because assurance independently checks the approach and reports concerns to the board. Project assurance is an independent check on the approach and reports to the board; it does not take over the team's testing.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An agile team on Project Harbor writes acceptance criteria on each backlog item, and Tomas Reyes accepts each increment. Sam Okafor wonders about a separate heavy acceptance document for each item. What should he do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Record the backlog acceptance in the quality approach and keep the registers current. Tailoring adapts the format, so criteria on backlog items and user acceptance can stand if recorded in the approach; the registers and independence remain.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the purpose of the quality practice? Answer: To create products that are fit for purpose and can be accepted by the users. Question two. Which activity checks products against their criteria? Answer: Quality control. Question three. Who carries out quality assurance? Answer: Project assurance or another function independent of the team that produces the product.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does the product register record? Answer: The products, their status and their approval. Question five. When are acceptance criteria agreed? Answer: Before the products are built. Question six. Where is the way quality will be achieved recorded? Answer: In the quality management approach, part of the initiation documentation.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Purpose: products fit for purpose and acceptable to users. Product description: purpose, composition, quality criteria and how checked. Quality register: every planned and completed check with result. Product register: products, status and approval. Quality control: checks the product, recorded. Quality assurance: independent check of the approach. Acceptance: by the right person, against criteria set before building. Tailoring: scales the paperwork, never the independence.
